full_judgment:
Md. Joynul Abedin, J : This Rule Nisi was issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh calling upon respondent Nos. 1 to 5 to show cause as to why the impugned letter No. DSE-433/2000/403 dated 1-3-2000 issued by the respondent No. 5, Chief Executive Officer of Dhaka Stock Exchange Ltd., should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and of no legal effect and also why respondent Nos. 1 to 5 should not be directed to act in pursuance of Regulation 7 of the Settlement of the Stock Exchange Transactions Regulations, 1998 in respect of transactions of 61,580 shares of Paper Processing and Packaging Limited of 30-12-1999. 

 3. Respondent No. 6 on the instruction of DSE deposited 61,580 shares of the petitioner with the clearing house of the DSE on 4-1-2000 which was duly received by it (DSE) on the same day. In terms of Regulations 7 and 8 of the Settlement of Stock Exchange Transactions Regulations, 1998 the petitioner was entitled to an amount of Taka 1,07,80,152.89 against buy and sale of various securities, including the sale proceeds of 61,580 shares by 12-1-2000, excluding the Hartal and Holidays. Even after the expiry of 6 days from the date of maturity of the above amount no payment was made to the petitioner. Accordingly, the petitioner on 18-1-2000 informed respondent No.6 of the matter in writing and respondent No. 6 in reply on 20-1-2000 stated that DSE failed to make payment to the account of respondent No. 6 due to Strike called by the Opposition Political Parties. Thereafter on 22-1-2000 the petitioner by another letter requested respondent No. 6 to inform the reason why the payment was not being made as per the Settlement Regulations and what steps were taken for obtaining payment from the DSE. Respondent No. 6 thereafter by a letter dated 25-1-2000 informed the petitioner that they never experienced such an instance of failure of the DSE in making due payment and requested the petitioner to have patience. The petitioner nonetheless again made a request to the respondent No. 6 by her letter dated 22-2-2000 for arranging the payment for the. sale proceeds due to her stating that she had to borrow in the meanwhile a large amount from their bankers due to non-receipt of the payment of the sale proceeds of the aforesaid shares and they were also compelled to sell out their stock of shares at a very lower rate to meet payments due from them for subsequent purchase against the sale of the shares of Paper Processing and Packaging Ltd. which turned to be a great burden on them. 

 13. There are yet other various ways under the said Ordinance and other connected laws by which the SEC controls the activities of the DSE to ensure that DSE acts in the affairs of SEC to help it protect the interest of the investors and develop the securities market and the matters ancillary thereto. SEC, where it is considered expedient, may direct the DSE to make regulations to carry out the purpose of the said Ordinance, 1969. Accordingly, Dhaka Stock Exchange Investors 'Protection Fund Regulations, 1999 and Settlement of Stock Exchange Transactions, 1998 are made by the DSE with the previous approval of SEC and these are all published in the official Gazette as empowered under section 34 of the Ordinance 1969. 

 17. In view of the Regulations 7 and 8 of the Settlement of Stock Exchange Transactions Regulations, 1998 the DSE has an obligation to pay up the outstanding amount of the sale proceeds of the shares to the petitioner through respondent No. 6 irrespective of the fact whether the respondent Nos. 8 and 9 paid for the said shares and the DSE could recover the full amount or not from the respondent Nos. 8 and 9. The word "Square-up" employed in Regulation 7 means that the DSE was and still is under obligation to make payment to the petitioner through respondent No. 6 for selling out the aforesaid shares of Paper Processing and Packaging Limited for the petitioner regardless of the fact whether the buyer member or members in this transaction defaulted to pay or not once the DSE obtained the share certificate of those shares from respondent No. 6 and also received its Laga and Howla charges from the petitioner. This position is also reaffirmed by the provisions under Regulation 8 of the said Ordinance. To hold otherwise would be contrary to and defeat the spirit and purpose of the enactment of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 and the Securities and Exchange Commission Act, 1993. These laws were made to ensure transparency and accountability in the affairs of the SEC and DSE to protect the interest of the investors like the petitioner in the present case and also to develop the capital and securities market in Bangladesh. Regulations 7 and 8 are reproduced below for appreciation. 

 "Regulation 7(i) If a member fails to deliver securities and/or make payment by cheque/pay order/demand draft within the settlement day, DSE shall automatically square up the unsettled transaction by buying in or selling out, as the case may be, in DSE after the day subsequent to the settlement day on the risk and account of the defaulting member, without any further reference. DSE shall inform the defaulting member as to the difference money, if any, for payment immediately after buying in or selling out by DSE." 

 "8 Clearance by delivery of securities and issue of cheque by DSE. The Clearing house shall deliver securities and make payment by account payee cheque to a member on the second day subsequent to the settlement day, ie T+5, in respect of the transactions carried out on each trading day."
